text: [...]A Paul Klee in prose--as delicate, as sly, as haunted. [...] Walser's [work is] charged with compassion: awareness of the creatureliness of life, of the fellowship of sadness. [...] As literature's present [...] remakes its past, we cannot help but see Walser as the missing link between Kleist and Kafka, who admired him greatly. [...] At the time [of Walser's writing], it was more likely to be Kafka [who was understood] through the prism of Walser. Robert Musil, another admirer among Walser's contemporaries, when he first read Kafka pronounced [him] "a peculiar case of the Walser type." The moral core of Walser's art is the refusal of power; of domination. [...] Walser's virtues are those of the most mature, most civilized art. He is truly a wonderful, heartbreaking writer."

title: Fortifications of Westerplatte
text: The Polish were granted access to the Westerplatte Peninsula by the League of Nations in 1924 to build a military transit depot (WST). Some of the conditions of granting the peninsula to the Polish were that they could not have more than 88 military personnel, and build fortifications. The peninsula was separated from the Free City of Danzig by a 2m tall brick wall that ran across the base of the peninsula. In the summer of 1933, Polish authorities decided to secretly begin building fortifications on the peninsula as the threat of German aggression became more real. The first fortifications were several concrete blockhouses, light shelters, and gun emplacements.

title: I Wrote You a Letter
text: The release of M83's previous album, Fantasy, in 2023, marked the debut of Gonzalez's independent music label, named Other Suns, powered by Believe Music. This label would later receive a couple of soundtracks composed by M83 (namely A Necessary Escape, for the 2025 film Dakar: Race Against the Desert, and Resurrection, for the homonymous film directed by Bi Gan), while also hosting studio albums of artists associated with the band, including Kaela Sinclair's Supraliminal and Benoît de Villeneuve's Soul Tuning, both in 2025. Concurrently, with M83's ninth studio album released, Gonzalez held an artistic priority of touring throughout North America and Europe, and with the conclusion of the shows, he began producing the aforementioned soundtracks and the next full-length album in 2024, in the continued vision of making cinematic soundscapes for "people to go on big adventures, to feel alive and to forget about the world", as he said in an interview by Clash Music about Fantasy.

title: Sławomir Pietrzyk
text: In the 2010 Polish local elections, he ran from the same committee again, winning 1,697 (5.32%) votes and reclaiming his mandate. He became a close associate of the incumbent mayor Jacek Majchrowski, and was nominated the Vice-Chairman of the city council in 2010. As the Vice-Chairman, he suspended his membership in Social Democracy of Poland and became a member of political association Friendly Kraków (Polish: Przyjazny Kraków), which entered a coalition with the Civic Platform. He ran for re-election in the 2014 and 2018 local elections, winning 1,288 (4.58%) and 1,774 (4.53%) votes respectively and maintaining his seat. In 2018, Gazeta Wyborcza described Pietrzyk as the left wing of mayor Majchrowski's movement, sympathetic to the Democratic Left Alliance.

title: Sławomir Pietrzyk
text: On 6 December 2021, Kraków City Council from the Civic Platform, Alicja Szczepańska, filed a formal complaint about Pietrzyk. She alleged that during a formal meeting with a Lwów delegation, Pietrzyk offered to have a sexual intercourse with her, and later encouraged her to have sexual relations with one of the Lwów deputies. On 10 January 2022, the Disciplinary Committee voted to remove Pietrzyk from the role of Vice-Chairman. Pietrzyk strongly rejected the allegations, arguing that he fell victim to political intrigue. Despite losing his position as Vice-Chairman, he remained a city council member for the rest of his term.

title: Sławomir Pietrzyk
text: On 2 June 2026, he announced his candidacy for the 2026 Kraków mayoral election, and was endorsed by Social Democracy of Poland. He was subsequently also endorsed by Joanna Senyszyn, the founder of New Wave party who became famous for her 2025 Polish presidential election run. He campaigned on issues affecting elderly citizens of Kraków, and made ambitious political promises, such as making the Kraków public transport free. The media ignored his candidacy, and in one public debate, only six seats were prepared, leaving Pietrzyk, the seventh candidate, unable to participate. Ultimately, he won 947 (0.37%) votes, finishing last. He expressed disappointment at his performance. At the same time, he stated his readiness to endorse one of the runoff candidates, although ultimately he remained undecided.

title: RKO Bushwick Theatre
text: In April 1912 the Bushwick Theatre was acquired by theatre magnate Benjamin Franklin Keith, and became a part of the Keith Circuit of vaudeville theatres. By the following July it had been rebranded B. F. Keith's Bushwick Theatre (BFKBT). Some of the vaudeville entertainers who appeared at the theatre under Keith included the Marx Brothers; comedian and singer Sophie Tucker; Ken Murray and his wife Charlotte LaRose; actresses Elsie Janis, Mrs. Leslie Carter, Valeska Suratt and Ione Bright; actor Berton Churchill in a Shakespeare act; minstrel show entertainer Eddie Leonard; female impersonator Julian Eltinge; and Mayme Remington and her all-black cast tap dancing troupe. The theatre was also occasionally used by touring stock theatre companies for performances of plays and musical theatre.

title: RKO Bushwick Theatre
text: By 1925 the BFKBT was offering screenings of silent films in addition to live entertainment. The theatre continued to operate as BFKBT until 1929 when it became the RKOBT; beginning in February of that year with a screening of the film Annapolis in conjunction a live variety theatre show. Live vaudeville entertainments paired with film screening continued into the 1930s with performers like opera singer Everett Marshall and the comic musical duo Arren and Broderick. The RKOBT continued to operate as a movie theatre until closing in 1969. The building was soon after converted into a church; becoming the Pilgrim Baptist Church. It was a church for a relatively short period in the 1970s.

title: Karl Mokaraka
text: Mokaraka stood at the 2023 New Zealand general election for Vision NZ, contesting the Panmure-Ōtāhuhu electorate. At the Ōtara Markets in August, he led a protest against Labour leader Chris Hipkins. Later that same month, Mokaraka heckled Prime Minister Christopher Luxon from behind a fence, while Luxon was giving a media briefing in Pakuranga. Mokaraka's back-and-forth exchange with Luxon, which lasted for several minutes, resulted in memes on social media. After another heckling of David Seymour at ACT's campaign launch, Mokaraka began to be described as a serial heckler, a label he rejects. Mokaraka told The New Zealand Herald that he was motivated to heckle at political events to represent whānau without a voice.

title: The Pines, Brighton
text: The Pines, Brighton was constructed in 1866 by local prolific builder and dairyman William Durrant on 4 hectares (10 acres) he owned in the Brighton Estate, between Middle and Outer Crescent, where he built seven cottages. The Pines was the second in a sequence of larger concrete houses built by Durrant and the first occupant was the squatter, Frank W. Desailly. By 1872 The Pines was used as a school known as Brighton College and it appears that a timber addition was constructed at the rear for this purpose. This school was initially conducted by John MacVean, then John Batten until 1881, and finally Arthur Backhouse until c. 1883.

title: The Pines, Brighton
text: The Pines, Brighton is a concrete house with a hipped slate roof and brick and timber sections at the rear. It is a mid-Victorian Italianate villa with rendered walls which are lightly scribed to imitate ashlar construction. It has moulded chimney caps, quoined front corners, a central front door and tall paired double hung windows on either side. A concave roofed front verandah was modified with a replacement frame, concrete floor, and turned posts. The eaves have an unusual continuous rendered under-mould. The interior of the main house has a timber floor, plastered walls and ceilings, deep cornices and deep timber window reveals. At the rear of the main house are two sections, one of brick construction and a later addition to the west is of timber construction. To the rear of the property are two concrete outbuildings with corrugated iron roofs. It is recorded that the concrete used to form the walls of the house and outbuildings consisted of lime binding sand and stones from the nearby foreshore. This was rammed in layers before a rendered finish was applied.

title: Lin Yuying
text: In the spring of 1923, Lin returned to Changsha as a technician and party branch secretary at the Wangluyuan Weaving Factory. On 28 May, he led a strike by the city's rickshaw pullers against an increase in the fees charged by vehicle owners, which succeeded on 5 June. On 1 June, he led rickshaw pullers in a demonstration in Changsha protesting against the killing of Chinese civilians by Japanese sailors. In the autumn, he became business manager and party branch secretary of the Anyuan Railway and Mining Workers' Consumer Cooperative and joined the work of the CCP's Anyuan district committee. On 1 May 1924, he served as chief marshal at the opening of the new building of the Anyuan Railway and Mining Workers' Club. He then travelled to the Soviet Union and, after arriving in Moscow at the end of October 1924, studied at the Communist University of the Toilers of the East.

title: Lin Yuying
text: Lin was recalled to China in May 1925 and worked for the CCP's Shanghai committee. That year, he joined the party group of the Shanghai General Labour Union and became secretary of the CCP's Yangshupu section committee. On 6 December 1925, he took part in a mass rally organised by the union and other groups on Qingyun Road against Duan Qirui and the Fengtian clique. While leading the marchers, he was seriously injured in a clash with soldiers and police, and a head wound left him with lasting migraines. In 1926, he served as secretary of the Yangshupu and then the Caojiadu section committees, and in April he became a member of the CCP's Shanghai district committee.

title: Lin Yuying
text: In January 1927, Lin went to Hankou, where he served as an adjutant and head of a special detachment of the military commission of the Wuhan Nationalist Government. During the July 1927 break between the Wuhan government and the communists, he ran a furniture shop that served as a secret liaison point for the party. In September 1927, on the orders of the CCP's Hubei committee, he, Wang Juexin and Shi Bingqian formed the party's East Hubei Special Committee. The committee led Autumn Harvest Uprisings in Daye, Yangxin and Echeng, which failed. He then served as secretary of the CCP's Qiaokou district committee and, from October, as secretary of the Wuchang municipal workers' committee.

title: Granite B
text: The difference from the old Tonghab camouflage is based on digital pixels. The background for the issuance of this new combat uniform is that U.S. military requests for uniform improvements began in 2004, and the project got on track in earnest when the Department of Defense accepted the plan to improve the new combat uniform in May 2009. At that time, the United States had already introduced ACU combat uniforms produced using digital pixels such as Universal Camouflage Pattern. For landscape and environment context, there were three test types: granite, pine, and rock, and the granite pattern, which is very common in the terrain of the Korean Peninsula, was finally selected. Unlike the existing uniform, the new combat uniform also enhanced the functionality of the uniform itself and was manufactured using advanced fibers. This Granite B combat uniforms began to be issued to the Army, Navy, and Air Force starting in 2014.

title: Granite B
text: During the parade on January 14, 2021, the Korea People's Army Ground Forces wore digital camouflage uniforms and combat boots similar to the desert-colored combat boots that the Republic of Korea Army recently began issuing. The shape and material of the pockets match the initial type of the Republic of Korea Armed Forces standard combat uniform, and the pattern is also in the form of a color inversion. There was also an article that said some Korean-Chinese merchants were involved in leaking Korean military camouflage patterns. However, until first quarter of 2022, these camouflage been provided to strategic forces and military parade units actively mobilized for propaganda. But in 2026, North Korean military wore digital camouflage uniform, similar to Granite B and EMR camouflage.
